column1: # Expected permission-gate decision, tab, command text. Both hooks must agree on every line.
# Blank lines and # lines are skipped. An empty command stands for a tool call with no command field.
# git writes are the user's alone
# Staging under another name, and the Windows executable spelling
# Rewrites of history or the working tree
# The read half of a verb that names both a read and a write
# Worktree creation touches nothing the user owns

column2: git worktree add ../wt && git commit -m x
git commit -m x; git worktree add ../wt

column1: # The boundary is a word edge, not a delimiter list, so quoting and paths do not smuggle a write
# A gated name inside a longer word is not an invocation
# Backgrounding from inside the shell, which run_in_background does where the harness can see it
# An ampersand that redirects, chains, calls or belongs to an argument is not backgrounding

column2: unzip $(gh run download 1 --dir out; echo out)/a.zip

column1: # An explicit read method makes field flags read-only again
# Driving CI is a write, but destroys nothing durable

column2: gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main -f env=prod

column1: # gh writes, including the glued flag form and the unmethoded field flag

column2: gh api -X GET repos/o/r -X DELETE repos/o/r

column1: # graphql cannot be told apart from a mutation without reading the query body
# Every gh invocation in the command has to pass

column2: gh run download 1 && gh pr merge 5
